original_test_intent: Read one verified sensor's supported threshold values over OOB and compare each readable raw value, after SDR conversion, with the independently reported sensor threshold state.
original_method: Retain raw Sensor/Event 0x04/0x27 <sensor number>, then parse the Table 35-9 readable-threshold mask followed by LNC, LC, LNR, UNC, UC and UNR byte positions instead of treating bytes 3 through 8 as unconditionally valid.
manual_activity: Project supplies the approved sensor identity, matched SDR and comparison tolerance; ordinary read-only collection needs no interactive write approval.
required_inputs: Verified BMC, channel and sensor number
Matched SDR record and sensor units/linearization
Independent sensor-list threshold field mapping and tolerance
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, BMC or OS logs
Validate completion and exact response length
Honor the readable-threshold mask before interpreting values
Do not set thresholds, hysteresis or event enables
agent_execution_scope: Verify BMC and bind the sensor number to one SDR
Validate completion, response length and readable mask
Preserve all six raw byte positions while decoding only readable fields
Convert readable values with the matched SDR
Compare named threshold fields with independently captured sensor-list output
Archive raw, decoded and no-mutation evidence
engineer_actions: Approve sensor mapping and comparison tolerance
Review unsupported or inconsistent threshold data

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek is unnecessarily pessimistic about command availability; the source's raw 0x04/0x27 request is standard and read-only once the sensor is verified.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use one secret-safe raw 0x04 0x27 <sensor number> request as defined by IPMI v2.0 Table 35-9; parse the readable-threshold mask and the ordered LNC, LC, LNR, UNC, UC and UNR positions, then compare only supported values after SDR conversion.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The OOB path, sensor-number input, response-byte comparison and 10/5 timing are preserved; duplicated Criteria text and log clearing are recorded as source defects.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a schema-aware read that binds raw positions to named thresholds, gates them through the readable mask, converts them through the same SDR, and reports per-field agreement with an explicit tolerance.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the source's byte-range comparison protocol-aware and auditable without modifying the Master.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: This proves readable threshold state only; it does not prove Set Sensor Threshold behavior, hysteresis, event enablement or physical event generation.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A high-level sensor list may round values or omit unsupported fields, so byte equality is not a valid cross-interface oracle after unit conversion.

project_override_considerations: A high-level API is equivalent only if it identifies the same sensor, exposes the readable mask or unsupported state and reports all supported thresholds with documented conversion/rounding.
expected_evidence: Readable-threshold mask and all ordered raw byte positions
Per-field decoded engineering values and conversion inputs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title, raw request and comparison step consistently require a threshold read. The duplicated/corrupted Criteria wording, imprecise unconditional byte comparison and log-clearing boilerplate are quality and completeness defects, not mutually incompatible source requirements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The command and response schema are defined. Sensor mapping, SDR conversion and comparison tolerance are normal Project readiness inputs; malformed or unsupported data becomes an execution result rather than a reason to invent values.

review_improvement: Uses the readable mask and named field order so unsupported positions cannot falsely pass or fail, and compares converted thresholds with explicit rounding tolerance.
independent_technical_reasoning: Table 35-9 returns a readable-threshold mask before six fixed threshold byte positions. A byte position can contain data even when its mask bit says the threshold is not readable, and high-level tools may round converted values. PASS therefore requires one verified sensor/SDR, mask-gated decoding and named per-field comparison in engineering units, not raw blanket equality or mere command success.
